reading.title: Rewilding Britain
reading.text: Rewilding, the idea of letting farmland return to nature, has caused considerable controversy in Britain. Supporters say that converting a small share of farms into wild land could reverse the decline in wildlife and make the countryside more diverse. Beavers, for example, are versatile engineers: their dams store water and slow down floods. Farmers, however, fear that the policy will divert money away from food production, and some argue that once land is abandoned the change may be irreversible. Both sides agree on one point: the current loss of species cannot continue.
